name: Imscriptive Subatomic Engineering

phase_0.boundary_condition: The Planck-scale FDE(∞) bilattice where all gauge interactions unify and the number of truth values becomes countably infinite.

⊢.justification: The uninitialized register ⊥ representing the absence of gauge charge or information before scale descent begins.

⊣.justification: The terminal anchor ⊤ representing the fully confined, color-neutral state where all information is resolved.

≻.justification: The forward morphism moving from atomic scales (FDE(2)) to nuclear (FDE(3)) and deeper, increasing the gauge group rank.

≺.justification: The reverse morphism restricting a deeper FDE(n) register to a shallower FDE(k), collapsing high-index middle values to the top pole.

⋈.justification: The composition of embeddings that maps a lower-rank truth lattice injectively into a higher-rank one.

⊙.justification: The identity state where the system resides at the scale-free correlation point, self-referential and invariant.

∈.justification: The co-multiplication that splits a unified state into distinct gauge charge arms (e.g., Red, Green, Blue) or truth-value branches.

∋.justification: The multiplication that reconstitutes distinct gauge charges into a single singlet or a contradictory B-state if charges conflict.

⊤.justification: The affirmative evaluation of a specific gauge charge (e.g., Red) as a proven middle value in the lattice.

⊥.justification: The negative evaluation where a specific gauge charge is constructively refuted or absent in the current configuration.

⊞.justification: The paradice state holding both a charge and its negation simultaneously, representing a coherent superposition or contradiction.

⊡.justification: The permanent, append-only record of an integer winding number that stabilizes the structure against deformation.

phase_2.failure_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.void_description: The vacuum state with no gauge charge or information (⊥).
phase_3.true_description: A constructively proven gauge charge or structural configuration (T).
phase_3.false_description: A constructively refuted gauge charge or absent configuration (F).
phase_3.both_description: A paradice state holding conflicting charges simultaneously, such as a superposition of Red and Anti-Red (B).

steps.domain_action: Initialize the system in the vacuum state, representing the absence of gauge information.
Establish the self-referential critical threshold where scale correlations are infinite.
Branch the unified state into two arms: one for affirmative gauge charges and one for refuted charges.
Descend the scale on the affirmative arm, moving from FDE(2) to FDE(3) and beyond.
Compose the embedding to inject the lower-rank lattice into the higher-rank lattice.
Affirm the existence of a specific gauge charge (e.g., Red) as a middle value.
Record the integer winding invariant that stabilizes this charge against deformation.
Reverse the scale on the refuted arm, restricting the deeper lattice to a shallower one.
Compose the restriction map to collapse high-index values to the top pole.
Refute the existence of a specific gauge charge, marking it as absent.
Hold both the affirmed and refuted charges simultaneously in a paradice state.
Rejoin the affirmative and refuted arms into a single verdict, fusing conflicts to B.
Anchor the system in the singlet confinement state, closing the boundary.
Return to the self-referential identity, completing the loop at the critical threshold.

phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Gauge group morphisms that communicate charge states between nested lattices.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: The integer winding invariants stored as append-only records in the IFIX register.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The monotonicity theorem that orders operations by descending scale and increasing truth-value count.
phase_5.alfs_store: The FDE(∞) direct limit serving as the canonical bootstrap store for infinite truth values.

phase_6.cycle_cost: The computational cost of embedding a finite lattice into a larger one.
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: A system with n truth values at a specific scale.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: A system with n+1 truth values at a deeper scale, preserving the previous structure.
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The embedding is injective and the restriction is a coarsening, conserving the total information content across the scale transition.

⊢=𐑦: Subatomic engineering implies a regime where scale distinctions collapse, allowing the boundary to encode the full bulk content as a single register.
⊞=𐑳: The assignment of distinct primitives (𐑸 and 𐑦) to opposing sides indicates an asymmetric distribution of counts.
⊡=𐑭: The assignment of the protection primitive ⊡ in this context implies an integer-winding invariant that stabilizes the role against continuous deformation to a trivial state.
⊙=⊙: The assignment of the primitive ⊙ explicitly denotes the critical phase where the system resides at the threshold with scale-free correlations.
⊥=𐑖: The assignment of a primitive chirality in subatomic engineering implies a structurally enforced, multi-axis configuration that maintains persistent orientational symmetry breaking beyond thermal fluctuations.
≻=𐑑: Subatomic engineering implies the fundamental restructuring of particle states or binding configurations, which corresponds to irreversible or semi-reversible bond formation and structural transformation.
≺=𐑬: The primitive ≺ denotes a polarity that implies a self-complementary interface where donor and acceptor roles coexist simultaneously.
⋈=𐑐: Subatomic engineering requires geometry-enforcing interactions with near-certainty to maintain structural fidelity.
⊤=𐑧: High barrier — kinetically frozen; requires external driving to rearrange
∈=𐑚: Subatomic engineering interactions typically propagate through localized clusters or motifs rather than remaining strictly single-bond or spanning the entire system globally.
∋=𐑵: Subatomic engineering requires the cooperative assembly of numerous components to achieve stable structures.
